assertion: Medicaid members in Oregon, Kentucky, and New Hampshire who do not meet new federal work rules will keep their coverage through June 30, 2027, after all three states said they will use a six-month federal grace period.
independent_value: KATU, LPM, Concord Monitor all report the opt-in through June 2027
measure: Medicaid work requirement hold harmless state decisions

assertion: Gov. Tina Kotek said more than 600,000 Oregonians would need to take action under the federal law and that up to a third would be likely to lose coverage "even if they qualify under the new rules,"
More than 180,000 Oregonians are estimated to be at risk of losing coverage
reason: Estimate; matches Statesman Journal (180,000); KATU cites an earlier 200,000 projection.

assertion: Kentucky's House Bill 2, which the Republican-led legislature passed over Beshear's veto, requires the state to implement the requirements no later than Jan. 1, 2027
inaccuracy: The article says the bill passed over Beshear's veto; the legislature overrode his vetoes of 12 sections (April 14, 2026), not a veto of the whole bill.

assertion: Urban Institute estimates about 166,000 people will drop off Medicaid in an average month in 2028 in Kentucky, and 3 million to 7 million nationally.
reason: Projection; matches Urban Institute via LPM and RWJF (3 to 7 million from work requirements alone; 4.9 to 10.1 million with more frequent checks).

assertion: Granite Advantage averaged about 59,000 members in 2025, but the New Hampshire Fiscal Policy Institute projects that up to 29,000 residents could lose Medicaid by 2028, largely because of the new rules.
inaccuracy: The article presents 29,000 as the projection without noting the state estimates only 6,300 residents will be affected by work requirements.

assertion: A legislative oversight committee approved the delay the week before the state announced it.
inaccuracy: The article says the week before; the Monitor says the committee approved 'late last week' and DHHS issued its statement Friday, i.e. the same week.
independent_value: Committee approval late week of Nov 16-20

assertion: About 417,000 of the state's roughly 1.7 million AHCCCS members could be subject to the rules; states have until Dec. 11 to tell CMS; at least 10 states and Washington, D.C., had announced plans to participate as of Nov. 23.
